messages.content: In plain English, what does idempotent mean in programming? Keep it to two short paragraphs.

In programming, idempotent means that performing an action multiple times has the exact same effect as performing it just once. If you run an idempotent operation ten times, the end result is identical to running it one time. This is crucial for reliability because it allows systems to safely retry failed operations without causing unintended side effects, like double-charging a customer or creating duplicate records.

A common example is a "GET" request in web APIs: fetching the same user profile repeatedly always returns the same data without changing anything on the server. In contrast, a "POST" request that creates a new user is not idempotent, because sending it twice would create two separate users. Idempotency ensures that retries and repeated calls are safe, predictable, and harmless to the system's state.
